info.title: Python TDD workflow with requirement-based code changes

parts.text:
"You are inspecting a Python project inside a container at /app.

READ ONLY. Do not create, modify or delete any file under /app.
Any write there invalidates this run.

A developer is about to work on the task described below.

\"
<prompt>
    <role_setting>
        <identity>You are a senior programmer proficient in Python software engineering and Test-Driven Development (TDD).</identity>
        <expertise>You excel at implementing requirements and refactoring code in small-step iterations under a Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflow.</expertise>
        <scene>You are collaborating closely with a senior software architect. The architect produces incremental requirement documents based on the functional gaps of the current code; you are responsible for understanding the content of this document and implementing the requirements to change the status of target tests from non-passed to passed.</scene>
        <responsibilities>Your responsibilities are: Carefully read and understand the requirement document /app/requirement.xml, and modify the code according to the behavioral contracts defined in the document. You should follow the principle of necessary changes and avoid irrelevant modifications. You are prohibited from executing test actively.</responsibilities>
    </role_setting>

    <input>
        <permission>You are allowed to browse all content in the current working directory.</permission>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/\\">The folder containing all source code for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/tests/\\">The folder containing all unit tests for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/requirement.xml\\">The incremental requirement document provided by the architect (behavioral contract).</item>
    </input>

    <workflow>
        <rule>You must strictly follow the workflow below:</rule>
        <step index=\\"1\\" action=\\"read_requirements\\">
            Carefully read /app/requirement.xml to deeply understand every requirement (including the source code involved, current state, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria).
        </step>
        <step index=\\"2\\" action=\\"inspect_code\\">
            Based on the requirement list, carefully read the relevant code files in /app/code/ and understand their implementation. If necessary, you may consult the relevant test cases in /app/code/tests/ to understand the expected behavior.
        </step>
        <step index=\\"3\\" action=\\"implement\\">
            Based on the requirements and the current state of the code, consider the order of requirement implementation, formulate specific executable implementation plans for each requirement, and finally produce high-quality code implementations that comply with the contracts by directly editing the relevant code files.
        </step>
    </workflow>

    <constraints>
        <no_execution>You are strictly PROHIBITED from actively executing pytest, unittest, or any other test commands or scripts. Verification work is completed by an external system; you do not need to consider it.</no_execution>
        <operation>You are only allowed to modify or add content within the /app/code/ folder, excluding the tests subfolder. It is strictly PROHIBITED to make any changes to the /app/requirement.xml file or the /app/code/tests/ folder.</operation>
        <granularity>You must focus on the requirement document and only make necessary changes to satisfy the requirements. You should not expand the scope on your own or over-develop.</granularity>
    </constraints>

    <output>
        <product>Your modified codebase (changes under /app/code/). Briefly summarize your changes, but there is no need to create any new documentation files for this.</product>
    </output>
</prompt>

\"

Read enough of /app/code to answer concretely, then name 3 to 5
plausible FUTURE tasks that could reasonably follow this one in THIS codebase.
Refer to real files, functions or modules you actually read. Do not solve the
task, and do not write any file."

61: def _ignore_unmatched_kwargs(f: Callable) -> Callable:
62:     """Make function ignore unmatched kwargs.
63: 
64:     If the function already has the catch all **kwargs, do nothing.
65:     """
66:     if _contains_var_kwarg(f):
67:         return f
68: 
69:     @functools.wraps(f)
70:     def inner(**kwargs):
71:         # filter out kwargs that are not part of the function signature
72:         # and transform them to the correct type
73:         filtered_kwargs = {key: _parse(value, key, f) for key, value in kwargs.items() if _is_kwarg_of(key, f)}
74:         return f(**filtered_kwargs)
75: 
76:     return inner
77: 
78: 
79: def _contains_var_kwarg(f: Callable) -> bool:
80:     """Tells whether the given callable contains a keyword argument."""
81:     return any(param.kind == inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD for param in inspect.signature(f).parameters.values())
82: 
83: 
84: def _is_kwarg_of(key: str, f: Callable) -> bool:
85:     """Tells whether the given `key` identifies a keyword argument of the given callable."""
86:     param = inspect.signature(f).parameters.get(key)
87:     return param is not None and (
88:         param.kind is inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY or param.kind is inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD
89:     )
90: 
91: 
92: def _parse(value: str, key: str, f: Callable) -> Any:
93:     """Parse a value to the correct type.
94: 
95:     Args:
96:         value: The value to parse.
97:         key: The name of the kwarg.
98:         f: The function to parse the value for.
99: 
100:     Returns:
101:         The parsed value.
102: 
103:     """
104:     if _is_str_kwarg_of(key, f) or _is_artifact_loaded(key, f) or _is_output_kwarg(key, f):
105:         return value
106:     try:
107:         type_ = _get_unannotated_type(key, f)
108:         loaded_json_value = json.loads(value)
109: 
110:         if not type_:
111:             return loaded_json_value
112: 
113:         _pydantic_mode = int(os.environ.get("hera__pydantic_mode", _PYDANTIC_VERSION))
114:         if _pydantic_mode == 1:
115:             return parse_obj_as(type_, loaded_json_value)
116:         else:
117:             return TypeAdapter(type_).validate_python(loaded_json_value)
118:     except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
119:         return value
120: 
121: 
122: def _get_function_param_annotation(key: str, f: Callable) -> Optional[type]:
123:     func_param_annotation = inspect.signature(f).parameters[key].annotation
124:     if func_param_annotation is inspect.Parameter.empty:
125:         return None
126:     return func_param_annotation
127: 
128: 
129: def _get_unannotated_type(key: str, f: Callable) -> Optional[type]:
130:     """Get the type of function param without the 'Annotated' outer type."""
131:     type_ = _get_function_param_annotation(key, f)
132:     if type_ is None:
133:         return None
134:     return unwrap_annotation(type_)
135: 
136: 
137: def _is_str_kwarg_of(key: str, f: Callable) -> bool:
138:     """Check if param `key` of function `f` has a type annotation that can be interpreted as a subclass of str."""
139:     if func_param_annotation := _get_function_param_annotation(key, f):
140:         return origin_type_issubtype(func_param_annotation, (str, NoneType))
141:     return False
142: 
143: 
144: def _is_artifact_loaded(key: str, f: Callable) -> bool:
145:     """Check if param `key` of function `f` is actually an Artifact that has already been loaded."""
146:     if param_annotation := _get_function_param_annotation(key, f):
147:         if (artifact := get_workflow_annotation(param_annotation)) and isinstance(artifact, Artifact):
148:             return artifact.loader == ArtifactLoader.json.value
149:     return False
150: 
151: 
152: def _is_output_kwarg(key: str, f: Callable) -> bool:
153:     """Check if param `key` of function `f` is an output Artifact/Parameter."""
154:     if param_annotation := _get_function_param_annotation(key, f):
155:         if param_or_artifact := get_workflow_annotation(param_annotation):
156:             return bool(param_or_artifact.output)
157:     return False
158: 
159: 
160: def _sanitize_param_name_for_python(param_name: str) -> str:
161:     """Convert kebab-case parameter names to snake_case for Python compatibility."""
162:     # Convert kebab-case (e.g., "a-but-kebab") to snake_case (e.g., "a_but_kebab")
163:     return re.sub(r'-([a-z])', lambda m: '_' + m.group(1), param_name)
164:

166: def _map_function_annotations(function: Callable, template_inputs: Dict[str, str]) -> Dict:
167:     """Parse annotations to substitute values from Argo for the function parameters.
168: 
169:     For Parameter inputs:
170:     * if the Parameter has a "name", replace it with the function parameter name
171:     * otherwise use the function parameter name as-is
172:     * use the Parameter loader if provided
173:     For Parameter outputs:
174:     * update value to a Path object from the value_from.path value, or the default if not provided
175: 
176:     For Artifact inputs:
177:     * load the Artifact according to the given ArtifactLoader
178:     For Artifact outputs:
179:     * update value to a Path object
180:     """
181:     if _contains_var_kwarg(function):
182:         return template_inputs
183: 
184:     function_kwargs: Dict[str, Any] = {}
185: 
186:     # Iterate over the _function parameters_ and map the template inputs to them
187:     # e.g. for `function=func(param: Annotated[int, Parameter(name="my-param")])`,
188:     # and template_inputs={"my-param": "5"}, the function_kwargs will be {"param": 5}
189:     for func_param_name, func_param in inspect.signature(function).parameters.items():
190:         # Sanitize parameter names from kebab-case to snake_case if needed
191:         sanitized_func_param_name = _sanitize_param_name_for_python(func_param_name)
192:         
193:         if param_or_artifact := get_workflow_annotation(func_param.annotation):
194:             if isinstance(param_or_artifact, Parameter):
195:                 if param_or_artifact.output:
196:                     function_kwargs[func_param_name] = get_annotated_output_param(param_or_artifact)

198:                     # Look for the parameter in template inputs using both original and sanitized names
199:                     param_value = None
200:                     if param_or_artifact.name in template_inputs:
201:                         param_value = template_inputs[param_or_artifact.name]
202:                     elif sanitized_func_param_name in template_inputs:
203:                         param_value = template_inputs[sanitized_func_param_name]
204:                     elif func_param_name in template_inputs:
205:                         param_value = template_inputs[func_param_name]
206:                     
207:                     if param_value is None:
208:                         raise RuntimeError(
209:                             f"Parameter {param_or_artifact.name if param_or_artifact.name else func_param_name} was not given a value"
210:                         )
211: 
212:                     function_kwargs[func_param_name] = load_param_input(param_value, param_or_artifact.loads)
213:             else:
214:                 function_kwargs[func_param_name] = get_annotated_artifact_value(func_param_name, param_or_artifact)
215: 
216:         elif not is_subscripted(func_param.annotation) and issubclass(func_param.annotation, (InputV1, InputV2)):
217:             # We collect all relevant kwargs for the single `Input` function parameter
218:             function_kwargs[func_param_name] = map_runner_input(func_param.annotation, template_inputs)
219: 
220:         else:
221:             # Use the kwarg value as-is, with kebab-case to snake_case conversion
222:             if sanitized_func_param_name in template_inputs:
223:                 function_kwargs[func_param_name] = template_inputs[sanitized_func_param_name]
224:             elif func_param_name in template_inputs:
225:                 function_kwargs[func_param_name] = template_inputs[func_param_name]
226:             else:
227:                 # If the parameter is not found, leave it as is to avoid breaking other cases
228:                 function_kwargs[func_param_name] = template_inputs.get(func_param_name, None)
229:     return function_kwargs
230: 
231: 
232: def _runner(entrypoint: str, template_inputs_list: List) -> Any:
233:     """Run the function defined by the entrypoint with the given list of kwargs.
234: 
235:     Args:
236:         entrypoint: The module path to the script within the container to execute. "package.submodule:function"
237:         template_inputs_list: A list of dicts with "name" and "value" keys, to be mapped to the kwargs of the function.
238: 
239:     Returns:
240:         The result of the function or `None` if the outputs are to be saved.
241:     """
242:     # import the module and get the function
243:     module, function_name = entrypoint.split(":")
244:     function: Callable = getattr(importlib.import_module(module), function_name)
245:     # if the function is wrapped, unwrap it
246:     # this may happen if the function is decorated with @script
247:     if hasattr(function, "wrapped_function"):
248:         function = function.wrapped_function
249: 
250:     # convert the template inputs list to a dict
251:     template_inputs: Dict[str, str] = {}
252:     for kwarg in template_inputs_list:
253:         if "name" not in kwarg or "value" not in kwarg:
254:             continue
255:         # sanitize the key for python
256:         key = cast(str, serialize(kwarg["name"]))
257:         value = kwarg["value"]
258:         template_inputs[key] = value
259: 
260:     function_kwargs = _map_function_annotations(function, template_inputs)
261: 
262:     # The imported validate_arguments uses smart union by default just in case clients do not rely on it. This means that if a function uses a union
263:     # type for any of its inputs, then this will at least try to map those types correctly if the input object is
264:     # not a pydantic model with smart_union enabled
265:     _pydantic_mode = int(os.environ.get("hera__pydantic_mode", _PYDANTIC_VERSION))
266:     if _pydantic_mode == 2:
267:         from pydantic import ConfigDict, validate_call  # type: ignore
268: 
269:         function = validate_call(config=ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True))(function)
270:     else:
271:         if TYPE_CHECKING:
272:             from pydantic.v1 import validate_arguments
273:         else:
274:             if _PYDANTIC_VERSION == 1:
275:                 from pydantic import validate_arguments
276:             else:
277:                 from pydantic.v1 import validate_arguments
278: 
279:         function = validate_arguments(config=dict(smart_union=True, arbitrary_types_allowed=True))(function)
280: 
281:     function = _ignore_unmatched_kwargs(function)
282: 
283:     output_annotations = _extract_return_annotation_output(function)
284: 
285:     if output_annotations:
286:         # This will save outputs returned from the function only. Any function parameters/artifacts marked as
287:         # outputs should be written to within the function itself.
288:         try:
289:             output = _save_annotated_return_outputs(function(**function_kwargs), output_annotations)
290:         except Exception as e:
291:             _save_dummy_outputs(output_annotations)
292:             raise e
293:         return output or None
294: 
295:     return function(**function_kwargs)
296: 
297: 
298: def _parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
